clue.text: Bad spirit -.fellow swallows a small measure

indicators.note: the fellow takes the small measure down inside himself, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: a don is a college fellow
an em is a small printer's measure of width

explanation.surface: An evil spirit, or a man gulping down a tot of drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A fiend or devil is a malevolent supernatural being.

clue.text: Black Beauty? Nobody's familiar, with it

explanation.surface: The famous horse in the novel, unknown to everyone.
explanation.walkthrough: Black Beauty is the horse in Anna Sewell's novel, a literally dark horse; a dark horse is also a contender of whom little is known.
explanation.definitionFit: A black horse is dark in colour; figuratively, an unknown competitor about whom people know little.

clue.text: Many a girl produces marvellous food

parts.note: M, the Roman thousand, stands for many
Anna is a girl's name

explanation.surface: Lots of young women make wonderful meals.
explanation.definitionFit: Manna was the miraculous food given to the Israelites in the wilderness.

clue.text: It's midday, .and I noted, no change

indicators.note: the letters given are to change into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Someone remarks that at twelve o'clock nothing has altered.
explanation.definitionFit: Noontide is an old word for twelve o'clock in the day.

clue.text: Record a rebellion

explanation.surface: A disc and an uprising named by the same number.
explanation.walkthrough: A single played at 45 rpm was called a forty-five; the Forty-Five is the 1745 Jacobite rising in Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: A 45 rpm single is a kind of vinyl disc, and the Jacobite rising of 1745 is known by its year.

clue.text: A line of dots you can hear

indicators.note: the phrase says the word for dots is taken as spoken

parts.note: flecks are small spots or dots

explanation.surface: A row of dots that is audible, like Morse code.
explanation.definitionFit: A flex is an electric cable, a kind of wire.

clue.text: Vanessa married lad after dissolution

indicators.note: when something dissolves it breaks up, so the letters given are reformed

explanation.surface: Vanessa wed a young man after a divorce.
explanation.walkthrough: Vanessa looks like a woman's name, but it is the butterfly genus that includes the red admiral.
explanation.definitionFit: The red admiral butterfly belongs to the genus Vanessa.

clue.text: Girl in line to stand up and complain

indicators.note: in a down clue standing up means the whole is read upwards, reversed
the girl goes inside the line

parts.note: RY is the abbreviation for railway, a line
Emma is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A girl in a queue rises to protest.
explanation.definitionFit: To yammer is to whine or grumble loudly.

clue.text: Tool put into operation

explanation.surface: An instrument used to carry out a plan.
explanation.definitionFit: An implement is a utensil or instrument; to implement is to carry out a plan.

clue.text: Sheep lap the river, in which water may be found

definitions.text: in which water may be found

indicators.note: to lap is to enfold, so the sheep wrap around the river

parts.note: ewes are female sheep
R is the abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: Sheep drink from the river, where water is.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lap' reads as sheep drinking, but it means wrap around.
explanation.definitionFit: Ewers are large jugs used to hold washing water.

clue.text: Orders' not reused become ineffective

indicators.note: to order things is to arrange them, so these letters are put into a new sequence

explanation.surface: Instructions that are never recycled lose their force.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Orders' looks like the plural noun but is the verb, arranging NOT REUSED into a new phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: A plant that has run to seed has stopped being productive, so the idiom means to decline or go to waste.

clue.text: Wood'. obtained from soft-hearted fellow

indicators.note: the fellow is given a soft heart, so the letter goes into the middle of him

parts.note: a male is a man or fellow
p (piano) is the musical abbreviation for soft

explanation.surface: Timber got from a kindly man.
explanation.definitionFit: Maple is a hardwood timber from the tree of that name.

clue.text: Card game from Bucks, they say

indicators.note: the phrase signals that the word for bucks is to be heard spoken rather than read

parts.note: harts are male deer, like bucks

explanation.surface: A card game that comes from Buckinghamshire, people say.
explanation.walkthrough: Bucks is also short for Buckinghamshire, an English county, which is the false trail.
explanation.definitionFit: Hearts is a trick-taking card game in which players avoid winning tricks containing that suit.

clue.text: Unemployment in which love may bloom

definitions.text: Unemployment in which love may bloom

parts.words: Unemployment in which love may bloom
parts.note: having no work is the plain sense; the flower love-in-..., an old name for the wild pansy, lets love bloom in that state

explanation.surface: Being out of work leaves time for romance to flower.
explanation.walkthrough: Love-in-idleness is an old English name for the wild pansy, so love literally blooms in it.
explanation.definitionFit: Being out of work is a state of inactivity, which is what the word names.

clue.text: Cheerful chap on the staff .

parts.note: jolly means cheerful
Roger is a man's name

explanation.surface: A happy man employed by the firm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the staff' looks like employment; it means flying from a flagstaff, as the pirate flag does.
explanation.definitionFit: The pirates' skull-and-crossbones flag is flown from a flagpole.

clue.text: Shot — one shot — in American tournament

parts.note: a round is a single shot of ammunition
Cock Robin in the nursery rhyme was shot with a bow and arrow

explanation.surface: A gunshot, then another, at a contest in the United States.
explanation.walkthrough: The nursery rhyme 'Who killed Cock Robin?' has the sparrow shooting him with an arrow.
explanation.definitionFit: A round robin, originally a US term, is a competition in which every player meets every other.

clue.text: … as is chap who's joined the association

annotationWithheld.why: '... as is chap who's joined the association' (5,4): its definition is borrowed from 13-down's 'on the staff' across the ellipsis; no word of this clue defines the flag
annotationWithheld.clue: … as is chap who's joined the association

clue.text: He used to work for breakers, by the 'sound of it

indicators.note: the phrase says we hear the word for breakers rather than see it spelt

parts.note: surf is the foam of waves breaking on a shore

explanation.surface: A man once employed by a demolition firm, it seems.
explanation.definitionFit: A serf was a medieval labourer bound to work his lord's land.

clue.text: Golly for love, but not in love

parts.note: Fancy! is an exclamation of surprise like Golly!
doing something for love means doing it free

explanation.surface: A doll offered free, but no romance involved.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone fancy-free has no romantic attachment.

clue.text: Intoxicated by the dance, have a drink

parts.note: high means intoxicated
a ball is a formal dance

explanation.surface: Drunk after the dance, take another glass.
explanation.definitionFit: A highball is a mixed spirit and soda served in a tall glass.

clue.text: Charged on the way back for wrongdoing

indicators.note: going back means the word for charged is read from right to left

parts.note: a live wire is electrically charged

explanation.surface: Someone accused of a crime while returning home.
explanation.definitionFit: Evil is wickedness or sin, the doing of wrong.

clue.text: Spotted in fine' battle formation

indicators.note: a battle formation is an arrangement, so these letters are drawn up in a new order

explanation.surface: Seen during a fine piece of military manoeuvring.
explanation.definitionFit: Flea-bitten describes a horse's coat flecked with small reddish marks.

clue.text: Push to alter the final result

indicators.note: to alter is to change, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Pressing for change in the outcome.
explanation.definitionFit: The upshot is the eventual outcome or conclusion.

clue.text: Plan to study some church 'architecture

parts.note: to con is to study or learn by heart
a spire is a tall feature of a church building

explanation.surface: A scheme to examine part of a church's design.
explanation.definitionFit: To conspire is to plot or scheme together.

clue.text: Firm has a way.'. .

annotationWithheld.why: 'Firm has a way . . .' (5): CO + A + ST, but its definition 'to progress without effort' is in 24-down's text across the ellipsis, so no word of this clue defines it

clue.text: Wary about strange material

indicators.note: the word for wary goes around the other piece, enclosing it

parts.note: shy means cautious or wary
odd means strange

explanation.surface: Being cautious about an unfamiliar fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: Shoddy is cloth made from shredded recycled wool.

clue.text: . : to progress without effort — that's what it means

explanation.surface: Moving along effortlessly is the gist.
explanation.definitionFit: To float along is to move without effort, and the gist of a remark is its meaning.

clue.text: What's at the bottom of all the wine bottles?

definitions.text: What's at the bottom of all the wine bottles?

indicators.note: in a down clue the bottom of each word is its final letter

explanation.surface: Asking what is left in the base of the wine bottles.
explanation.definitionFit: Lees are the sediment of yeast and solids that settle in wine.

clue.text: First of all, try to put out of countenance

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the word all is used

parts.note: to have a bash is to have a try

explanation.surface: Above everything, attempt to disconcert someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First of all' reads as 'firstly', but it asks for the first letter of 'all'.
explanation.definitionFit: To put someone out of countenance is to embarrass or disconcert them.

clue.text: Soldier of the king turned European? That's right

parts.note: GR is Georgius Rex, King George

indicators.note: turned means the word for the European is read backwards

parts.note: a Dane comes from Denmark
i.e. (id est) means that is

explanation.surface: Was a royal soldier converted to Europe? Correct.
explanation.definitionFit: Grenadiers are infantrymen, originally those who threw grenades.

clue.text: Follow each other and act in scenes from a film

definitions.text: act in scenes from a film

explanation.surface: Go one after another, and perform for the camera.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits the phrase: a take is a filmed scene and turns are acts, so performers doing their acts in takes take turns.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something in rotation is alternating, one after another; humorously, putting on acts in film shots.

clue.text: Fired ammunition that's plastic

parts.note: lit means set alight, fired
HE is high explosive, a type of ammunition

explanation.surface: Ammunition that was shot is made of plastic.
explanation.definitionFit: Plastic in its sense of pliable or supple, easily bent.
